title: solutions-pro-services-weekly-sync-notes-2026-04-14
content:
Solutions + Pro Services Weekly Sync — 2026-04-14

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (owner)
- Diego Alvarez
- Priya Patel
- Samir Rao
- Laura Kim
- Evan Brooks (customer success liaison)
- + recorded dial-ins from customer engineers (Acme Health, BrightBank)

Agenda:
1) Quick round-robin customer statuses
2) Blockers that need engineering escalation
3) Deployment/infra coordination (VPC, certs, routing)
4) Action items & owners

High-level summary:
- Progress continues across the top 3 integrations (Acme Health, BrightBank, OmniRetail).
- Biggest open risk is Acme Health network auth / VPC peering flakiness (intermittent) and a model mismatch issue for BrightBank (version pin vs. runtime behavior).
- We confirmed timeline for OmniRetail Dedicated rollout: can start limited production traffic next week if smoke tests pass.

Customer-specific notes:
1) Acme Health (regulated healthcare customer)
- Status: in staging, moving towards UAT.
- Current issues: intermittent failures when pulling large-context requests across the peered VPC (requests drop ~2-3% during peak 10:00-11:30 PST).
- Troubleshooting: infra ran tcpdump and saw retransmits between Redwood Private egress and Acme's transit gateway. Network team suspects MTU or intermittent route flaps.
- Tickets: PROJ-4321 (Acme VPC peering investigation), PROJ-4338 (staging smoke failures).
- Temporary mitigation: increase client-side retry window and add jitter; disable large-batch requests for the next 48 hours.
- Blocker severity: P2 (customer UAT delay risk).
- Next steps: Diego to coordinate with infra (network) and Acme network ops; Samir to prepare rollback plan for recent kernel-level NIC driver update in staging. Target: diagnostic update by 2026-04-16.

2) BrightBank (financial customer on Redwood Dedicated)
- Status: functional in sandbox, customer reported hallucination regression in a small prompt family after model upgrade.
- Root cause: model variant used in dedicated pool was v2.1-quant; customer's evaluation set shows higher hallucination rate vs pinned v2.0.
- Tickets: PROJ-4390 (BrightBank model regression), GH PR: integration-scripts#58 (adds evaluation harness).
- Decision: rollback the dedicated pool to v2.0-quant for BrightBank's route while we run a focused eval on v2.1.
- Action: Priya to run targeted eval and produce quality delta report by 2026-04-15; Laura to schedule canary traffic test if results are acceptable.

3) OmniRetail (SaaS customer)
- Status: Dedicated rollout preparing for limited prod traffic.
- Checklist: infra readiness ✅, model pinned ✅, routing rules ✅, canary policy configured ✅.
- Open: runbook for auto-fallback to Hosted API if Dedicated pool saturates (need SRE sign-off).
- Action: Evan to confirm SLA implications and get sign-off from SRE by 2026-04-17.

Cross-cutting technical notes:
- Certificate rotation: customers on Private deployments need to rotate client certs next week; we sent guidance to all affected accounts. Action: Maya to follow up on confirmations by 2026-04-16.
- Observability: added a custom dashboard for per-route 95th latency and token costs; useful to show customers during UAT demos.
- Billing/usage: BrightBank asked for a temporary detailed cost breakdown for dedicated test runs (they want per-token + infra amortization). Finance okayed a one-off export.

Blockers requiring escalation:
- Acme VPC flaps (PROJ-4321) — needs infra networking team deep-dive, potential escalation to cloud provider if we see route instability. Owner: Diego.
- Model regression for BrightBank (PROJ-4390) — requires Research/Applied ML involvement to profile v2.1 changes; owner: Priya.
- Auto-fallback runbook outstanding — SRE sign-off required (Evan to chase).

Decisions made in this meeting:
- BrightBank: rollback to v2.0-quant on Dedicated pool until eval completes.
- OmniRetail: proceed with limited production traffic on 2026-04-21 if canary passes.
- Acme: hold large-batch traffic for 48 hours; use retries/jitter as stopgap.

Action items (owner — due):
- Diego: coordinate network deep-dive for PROJ-4321, include cloud provider ticket if instability persists — due 2026-04-16.
- Priya: run targeted eval for BrightBank prompts comparing v2.0 vs v2.1, produce quality delta report (metrics: hallucination rate, factuality score) — due 2026-04-15.
- Samir: prepare NIC rollback plan for staging and test in dev cluster — due 2026-04-16.
- Laura: plan canary traffic schedule for BrightBank rollback/upgrade testing and notify customer — due 2026-04-17.
- Evan: get SRE sign-off on auto-fallback runbook for OmniRetail Dedicated rollout — due 2026-04-17.
- Maya: confirm certificate rotation completions with affected Private customers and collect confirmations — due 2026-04-16.

Notes / Conversation snippets (raw):
- "Acme saw the spike right after the NIC driver update — looks correlated but not yet causal" — Samir.
- "We don't want to expose BrightBank to v2.1 until we have hard eval numbers" — Priya.
- "If OmniRetail goes live, watch 95th latency and model warm-up token cost closely first 24h" — Diego.

Risks / open questions:
- If Acme network instability persists, UAT schedule may slip by 1-2 weeks. Are we ok with pushing their go-live? (product + CS to decide).
- BrightBank is sensitive to hallucination regressions; do we require automated acceptance tests before any model-roll change on Dedicated? (proposal: require eval pass + canary at 1% traffic for 48h).

Follow-ups / Where to find artifacts:
- Acme integration spec + recent logs: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PRO/Acme+Health+Integration
- BrightBank eval PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/integration-scripts/pull/58
- Open tickets: JIRA PROJ-4321, PROJ-4338, PROJ-4390
- Slack channel: #solutions-pro-services (thread pinned messages include runbooks and checklists)

Next meeting:
- Weekly sync: 2026-04-21 09:00 PST (same calendar invite). Expect status updates on PROJ-4321, PROJ-4390, and OmniRetail canary.

Notes to self / informal:
- Prep a short one-pager for product about potential scheduling slip for Acme; include mitigation options (extra infra capacity, temp Hosted fallback).
- Remind CS to surface any legal/regulatory checklist items from Acme as they finalize UAT criteria.

-- Maya C.
